 NFL Week 7 grades: Falcons earn solid 'A' mark, while Panthers flop with a resounding 'F'
 We're grading every game from Week 7 that has been played so far
 By
 John Breech 
 Oct 25, 2026
 at
 11:23 pm ET 
 •
 19 min read
 Add CBS Sports on Google 
 Getty Images 
 Welcome to the Week 7 grades!
 We have somehow hit the final Sunday of October, and when you look at the NFL standings , there are definitely a few surprises. For one, the Cleveland Browns are in first place in their division. I repeat, the Cleveland Browns are in first place. This is not a drill. One reason the Browns' magical run is happening is because of Deshaun Watson . 
 During Cleveland's 27-24 win over Tennessee, Watson engineered another fourth-quarter game-winning drive on Sunday, and he now has five on the season. That makes him just the third QB since 1970 to have a game-winning drive in each of his team's first five wins of a season. 
 Not to be outdone, the New York Giants are also in first place of the NFC East, AND they just won a game with J.J. McCarthy as their starting quarterback. If I had told you in August that the first-place Giants were going to win a Week 7 game with J.J. McCarthy under center, I would have been laughed at on the internet. No one's laughing now. 
 The Giants have now won a game with three different starting quarterbacks this year (McCarthy, Jameis Winston and Jaxson Dart ). That makes them the first team since the 2016 Patriots to win at least three games with three different starters before November. 
 On the other side of the standings, the Baltimore Ravens are in last place after suffering one of the most shocking losses in NFL history. The Ravens led the Bengals 13-0 at halftime but ultimately lost 35-13. 
 That's the third-largest loss in NFL history by a team that led by at least 13 points at halftime. 
 Since 2020, the Ravens have lost 17 games in which they led by double digits at some point, the most in the NFL in that span. All three of their losses this year have come in games where they held a double-digit lead. 
 This was the second straight week where they shut out their opponent in the first half, only to go scoreless and lose in the second half. 
 To make matters worse for the Ravens, the two teams we mentioned earlier -- the Giants and Browns -- are coached by two people the Ravens got rid of at the end of last season (John Harbaugh and Todd Monken). 
 With that in mind, let's get to the grades, starting with Baltimore's ugly loss. 
 Bengals (4-2) 35-13 over Ravens (4-3)
 B+ 
 Bengals
 The Bengals had their ugliest first half of the season, but they more than made up for it by destroying the Ravens over the final two quarters. The offense totaled just 59 yards in the first half, but then Joe Burrow came out on fire after halftime. He went 16-of-18 for 249 yards and four touchdowns in the second half alone. The only reason the Bengals were in the game heading into halftime is that the defense saved the day. The Ravens had two red zone trips in the first two quarters, and the defense held them out of the end zone each time. The defense also came up with a clutch fourth-down stop in the fourth quarter with the Bengals clinging to a 14-13 lead. If the Bengals play the rest of the season as they did in the second half, there's no reason they can't win the AFC North.  
 D- 
 Ravens
 This was a total second-half meltdown by a Ravens team that watched a 13-0 halftime lead turn into a 22-point blowout loss. Jesse Minter is suddenly starting to have the same problems that John Harbaugh used to have: He's blowing big leads. For the second straight week, the Ravens blew a double-digit lead and ended up losing. All three of their losses this year have come in a game where they led by double digits. In this game, Minter gambled and lost in the fourth quarter on a fourth-down play where he decided to go for it. The Ravens had a chance to take the lead with a short field goal, but instead, they had Tyler Huntley throw a pass, and it went incomplete. If Lamar Jackson is your QB, it probably makes sense to go for it there, but if you have a backup in the game and a chance to take the lead in the fourth quarter, just take the points. This is a painful loss for a Ravens' team that's now 0-2 in division play.  
 Seahawks (3-4) 20-3 over Chiefs (5-1)
 D- 
 Chiefs
 This game was a matchup nightmare for the Chiefs. The Seahawks went all-in on stopping Kenneth Walker, which should have opened things up for Patrick Mahomes, but Kansas City's receivers couldn't get any separation from Seattle's secondary. And if you throw in the fact that Mahomes was under intense pressure all night, this led to a game where the Chiefs essentially had no chance. You don't often see the Chiefs get bullied like this, but it happened here. It also didn't help that Harrison Butker killed Kansas City's chances of getting back in the game with two missed field goals. The Chiefs ran into a buzzsaw here, and they got beat by a team that thoroughly outplayed them.  
 A 
 Seahawks
 It's not often that you see a team completely dominate the Chiefs, but that's exactly what the Seahawks did here. This was a defensive masterpiece by Mike McDonald: In the Kenneth Walker revenge game, the Seahawks bottled up their former running back, holding him to just 36 yards on 14 carries. They dared the Chiefs to throw the ball and they dared the Chiefs to beat them with any other weapon, but Kansas City couldn't do it. The Seahawks defense was so good that the Chiefs' offense didn't reach the red zone a single time, marking the first time that's ever happened in Patrick Mahomes' career. And let's not forget about Jaxon Smith-Njigba (nine catches, 150 yards), who continues to be the most uncoverable receiver in the NFL. The Chiefs knew he would be getting the ball, but they still couldn't stop him. Yes, the Seahawks have three losses, but if they keep playing like this, we might actually see them make a return trip to the big game. The team that played Sunday night can win it all.   
 Lions (4-2) 20-17 over Packers (4-3)
 B 
 Packers
 The Packers might need a new kicker. They thought they had their kicker of the future in rookie Trey Smack after he hit his first five field goal attempts of the season, but he's fallen apart since then. Smack missed two field goals from inside 35 yards and that was the difference in the game. Of course, this loss wasn't all Smack's fault; there was plenty of blame to go around. There was a failed fourth down at Detroit's 7-yard line, Jordan Love threw a fourth-quarter interception, and Green Bay's defense let the Lions convert 50% of their third-down attempts. And let's not forget about the Packers' rushing attack. It was dead last in the NFL going into this game and the return of Josh Jacobs didn't make things any better. Jacobs was a weapon in the passing game -- he caught five passes for 55 yards -- but the Packers still can't run. It's going to be hard for this team to beat good teams if this offense continues to be completely one-dimensional.  
 B 
 Lions
 There's a fine line between being aggressive and being crazy, and Dan Campbell was certainly walking it in this game. Campbell had the Lions go for it on fourth-and-1 from their own 24 in the fourth quarter, and although they failed, Detroit's special teams bailed Campbell out by tipping the kick and knocking it off course. And that was the story of the day for the Lions: Whenever they needed someone to come up with a big play, they got it. The offense was firing on all cylinders with Jared Goff (303 passing yards), Jahmyr Gibbs (116 rushing yards) and Amon Ra St. Brown (153 receiving yards) all going off. The Lions defense came through with its best performance of the season, holding an opponent under 21 points for the first time all year. This was a well-rounded win by a Lions team that's undefeated at home this season (3-0).  
 Rams (3-4) 35-21 over Raiders (3-4)
 A- 
 Rams
 The Rams were so good in this game that they essentially had it locked up before halftime. Everything was clicking for Sean McVay and a Rams' offense that couldn't be stopped: Blake Corum and Kyren Williams combined to average 6.4 yards per carry during the first two quarters. As if that wasn't enough, Matthew Stafford opened up the game by completing 17 of his first 19 passes for 148 yards and three touchdowns. This was a game that the Rams couldn't afford to lose, and that's exactly how they played. At 2-5, it would have been panic time, but instead, they're now 3-4 with the Chargers, Commanders and Cardinals on deck. This team is now positioned to get right back in the playoff race.  
 C- 
 Raiders
 The Raiders' season got off to a fun start, but if we've learned one thing over the past four weeks, it's that they're not quite good enough yet to take down the best teams in the NFL. The Raiders defense had no answers for anything the Rams did. The Raiders were trailing 28-3 before this game even reached halftime, and at that point, the result felt inevitable. With the Raiders on a four-game losing streak, you have to start to wonder whether this team will soon think about replacing Kirk Cousins with Fernando Mendoza.  
 Broncos (5-2) 30-16 over Cardinals (2-5)
 B+ 
 Broncos
 The Broncos have struggled to run the ball this season, but they finally got things going here, and it was mostly thanks to Bo Nix. Through the first few weeks of the season, Nix has seemed a little hesitant to run, but that changed on Sunday. He scrambled seven times for 74 yards, including a wild 62-yard TD run in the second quarter that gave Denver the lead for good. Rookie Jonah Coleman was a pleasant surprise for Denver, averaging 6.0 yards per carry on nine rushes. Since Nix took over as the QB in 2024, the Broncos are now 12-0 when they top 125 rushing yards, so carrying this momentum forward will be important.  
 C 
 Cardinals
 If you're wondering why the Cardinals are 2-5, all your questions were answered in this game. With a sputtering Broncos offense coming to town, this could have been a big game for the Cardinals, but instead, their defense got torched. The Cards' surrendered multiple plays, including three that went for at least 45 yards. On offense, the Cards' were surprisingly successful between the 20s, but they couldn't do anything in the red zone. They made five trips inside Denver's 20, but came away with just one touchdown. Trey McBride continues to be the most unstoppable tight end in the NFL right now, but the Cards' don't have anyone else on offense that frightens the other team.  
 Falcons (3-4) 29-20 over 49ers (6-1)
 C 
 49ers
 This was a sloppy game by a team that doesn't usually play sloppy football. Brock Purdy threw multiple interceptions in a game for the first time since November 2025. Rookie running back Kaelon Black didn't help things by losing a fumble inside Atlanta's 30-yard line. The 49ers piled up 400 yards of offense, but a lot of that went to waste thanks to four turnovers. The 6-0 start was nice, but now, the 49ers suddenly look mortal, and they'll likely have a bad taste in their mouth heading into their Week 8 bye.  
 A 
 Falcons
 The Falcons won this game because their defense did something that no other team has been able to do this year: slow down the 49ers' offense. This was an all-time group effort with multiple players coming up big, including Jessie Bates III (one interception, one forced fumble), Kendal Daniels (one interception), Xavier Watts (one forced fumble), Maason Smith (one sack, one forced fumble) and Za'Darius Smith (one sack). The Falcons forced a total of four turnovers that led to 13 points, and that was the difference in the game. We know this offense is good, and if the defense is playing at the same level, this team could be very dangerous going forward. The Falcons just proved that they can go toe-to-toe with any team in the NFL. 
 Vikings (6-0) 16-10 over Colts (2-5)
 C 
 Colts
 The Colts had a kicker problem and a QB problem on Sunday, but otherwise, they played well enough to knock off the undefeated Vikings . On the kicking end, Spencer Shrader missed two field goals (48, 56), including a fourth-quarter kick that would have tied the game. On the QB end, Daniel Jones looked completely uncomfortable against a Vikings defense that had him on the run for most of the game while sacking him four times. Jones had a chance to lead a potential game-winning drive, but he threw an interception with his final pass of the game.  Jonathan Taylor  actually found some running room against the Vikings, and Indy's defense did its job, but Jones didn't pull his weight. At 2-5, the season isn't over for the Colts, but if they lose in Week 8 to the Jaguars , it might be time to blow things up.  
 B- 
 Vikings
 The Vikings have been riding their defense to victory all season, and this week was no different. Blake Cashman was the star against the Colts: He had two sacks, multiple QB hits and he led all players in the game with 12 tackles. Daniel Jones will probably be having nightmares about Cashman. When your defense is this dominant, you just need a small spark from your offense to win games, and Minnesota got that from Kyler Murray in the fourth quarter. Murray totaled 80 yards in the final quarter, including a 35-yard run that set up a 5-yard TD pass to T.J. Hockenson that provided the game-winning points. The offense is still an issue, but it's been looking better every week, and that's what the Vikings need to see.  
 Giants (4-2-1) 27-21 over Texans (2-5)
 A- 
 Giants
 John Harbaugh looks like a genius. The Giants' coach decided to bench Jameis Winston this week and turn the offense over to J.J. McCarthy, and the gamble paid off big time. McCarthy was in total control of the offense, and he quickly formed chemistry with  Malik Nabers , who caught seven passes for 111 yards. McCarthy also got some help from a Giants' rushing attack that totaled 188 yards on the ground. Harbaugh made sure to get Cam Skattebo involved in the offense this week. After getting zero carries in Week 6, the running back redeemed himself with a big game here that saw him rush for 124 yards. This team suddenly looks good enough to win the NFC East.  
 B- 
 Texans
 Houston, we have a problem, and it's a problem that no one could have predicted going into the 2026 season: The Texans ' defense is bad. The unit was the best in the NFL last year, but things have changed this season. For the third time in seven games, the Texans gave up at least 400 yards. They couldn't stop the run, and they gave up multiple big plays, including a game-winning 30-yard TD run by Devin Singletary in overtime. The offense isn't good enough to carry this team without some help from the defense, and that help just isn't there right now. The Texans just lost all the momentum they gained from their Week 6 win over the Jaguars.  
 Buccaneers (2-5) 43-13 Panthers (3-3)
 A+ 
 Buccaneers
 The Buccaneers realized early in the game that they could run on the Panthers , so they pounded the rock all day. From Bucky Irving (106 yards) to Kenneth Gainwell (88 yards) to Sean Tucker (52), the Bucs absolutely steamrolled the Panthers on the ground to the tune of 258 yards, the team's second-highest rushing total over the past 10 years. Defensively, the Bucs have been quietly playing good football all year, and that continued here. Yaya Diaby terrorized Bryce Young on a day when he racked up three of Tampa's five sacks. There was also a TD by Calijah Kancey , who returned a fumble for a score.  This was a statement win by the Bucs, and the statement is that they are still very much alive in the NFC South race.  
 F 
 Panthers
 This team gave up 59 points in Week 1, but that wasn't even their worst performance of the season. This was. It was a nightmare day all around for the Panthers. Bryce Young has looked good all season, but he regressed here with three turnovers, including a fumble that got returned for a TD. The defense got trampled for more than 250 yards on the ground. This was a total no-show by the Panthers, and they need to make sure it doesn't happen again going forward.  
 Browns (5-2) 27-24 over Titans (1-6)
 B 
 Browns
 Browns coach Todd Monken got ripped for giving the starting QB job to Deshaun Watson back in August, but right now, he looks like a genius. Watson pulled off another game-winning drive in the fourth quarter, marking the fifth time this year he's done that. In the game's final quarter, he went 6-of-9 for 76 yards, including a 36-yard pass to Harold Fannin that helped set up Andre Szmyt's game-winning kick. The Browns topped 400 yards of offense for the first time this season, and if you combine that with how well this defense is playing, it's starting to feel like the Browns might be a big part of the playoff conversation going forward.  
 B- 
 Titans
 The  Titans  blew a 14-0 lead because the offense choked and the defense totally disappeared in the fourth quarter. The offensive problems started in the second quarter after a possession where the Titans got zero points after getting stuffed on three straight plays from the Browns' 1-yard line. You have to score there. On top of that, Cam Ward's never-ending struggles continued with an interception, and the Titans also saw rookie Carnell Tate lose a rare fumble. To add insult to injury, Robert Saleh's defense couldn't get a single stop in the fourth quarter. Due to the loss, Tony Pollard's monster performance (129 yards, three touchdowns) went to waste. The Titans have now gone 65 straight games without picking up back-to-back wins. This is a frustrating team to watch.  
 Dolphins (1-5) 28-25 over Jets (2-5)
 A- 
 Dolphins
 The Dolphins offense has struggled this season, but Miami came out firing in this game. Malik Willis was sharp in the first quarter, completing 6-of-8 passes for 84 yards while leading the Dolphins on two TD drives. The offense has been slowly improving this year, and it's not just Willis. Running back Ollie Gordon has become a weapon (he topped 100 yards against the Jets ). Rookie receiver Caleb Douglas is also starting to shine: He had 70 yards and two touchdowns. Look, this team isn't going to the playoffs, but if you're Jeff Hafley, you just want to see some improvement every week, and the Dolphins certainly showed some here. 
 C 
 Jets
 This was a choke job by a Jets team that may have overlooked the Dolphins, who were winless heading into this game. The Dolphins had only scored 26 points in the first half ALL SEASON, but they put up 21 against the Jets. There was no pressure on Malik Willis, and he took advantage by picking apart the Jets in the first half. There were some solid individual performances with Braelon Allen topping 100 rushing yards and Omar Cooper topping 100 receiving yards, but overall, this was a poor showing. If Aaron Glenn wasn't on the hot seat before the game, he should be now.  
 Steelers (5-2) 16-10 over Saints (2-5) in Paris
 B 
 Steelers
 Every Steelers win seems to be the same: This team won't wow you, but they get the job done. On defense, the Steelers suffocated the  Saints'  ground game, holding New Orleans to just 18 yards rushing.  Payton Wilson , who had a red-zone interception, was one of several players who came up big for a Steelers defense that shut out the Saints in the second half. Offensively, the Steelers played efficient, mistake-free football. Jaylen Warren hit 100 rushing yards for the third time in the past five weeks, and the Steelers have gone 3-0 when that happens.  Aaron Rodgers  did a good job of getting all of his pass-catchers involved, and he showed that he still has his long ball with a 51-yard pass to  DK Metcalf  that came on Pittsburgh's only TD drive of the game. This team has quietly climbed to the top of the AFC North, and they might be there for a while.  
 C 
 Saints
 This loss basically summed up everything that's wrong with the Saints this year. Going into Week 7, they had given up the third most rushing yards per game in the NFL, and it was more of the same here with the Steelers running through New Orleans for nearly 150 yards. The Saints also ranked in the bottom six of the NFL in allowing opponents to convert on third down, and yup, the Steelers dominated them there, converting 62.5% of their third-down attempts. The Saints' star on offense was  Tyler Shough , but he got no help from a nonexistent rushing attack that totaled just 18 yards. With Shough carrying the offensive load, he couldn't afford to make any mistakes, but he ended up making one with a red zone interception after a seven-minute drive to start the second half. This team has a lot of issues, especially on defense, and it's hard to see them getting fixed anytime soon.  
 Bears (5-2) 30-24 over Patriots (4-3)
 B- 
 Patriots
 The Patriots have been a completely different team on the road this year, and that's not a good thing for New England. They're now 1-3 away from home after losing on Thursday night, and their problem in Chicago was that their defense couldn't come up with a stop. In the fourth quarter alone, the Patriots let the Bears convert a third-and-9 from their own 10, a third-and-11 from their own 10 and a fourth-and-2. If you want to win big games, you have to make big plays, and the Patriots' defense simply didn't do that in crunch time. The Patriots are now 0-8 in Drake Maye's career when their opponent scores at least 30 points.  
 B+ 
 Bears
 After throwing for 305 yards in his return to the field in Week 6, Caleb Williams topped himself against the Patriots by throwing for 308. One thing Williams has thrived at is spreading the ball around. The Bears had five different players catch at least four passes, which kept the Patriots' defense guessing all night. Before the season, Ben Johnson predicted a big year for Luther Burden, and it's easy to see why the Bears' head coach has so much faith in the second-year receiver. Burden went off for 130 yards, which all came in the first half. Except for one illegal trick play, Johnson was in his bag. He always seemed to have his offense running one step ahead of Mike Vrabel's defense. The Bears scored 59 points in Week 1, but it feels like this offense still hasn't hit its peak. With Williams back under center, the sky is the limit for Chicago.
